title: Antibiotic effects on gut-derived short chain fatty acid pools in healthy volunteers.
authors: Shremo Msdi Abdulwhab; Ayele Hossaena; Begum Khurshida; Hu Chenlin; Jo Jinhee et al.
summary_zh: 本研究通过纵向分析健康志愿者抗生素暴露后粪便样本，发现万古霉素全面抑制短链脂肪酸池，且对线性短链脂肪酸抑制更显著。
innovation: 纵向刻画抗生素对线性和支链短链脂肪酸池动态的影响 | 揭示万古霉素对纤维发酵相对于氨基酸发酵的不成比例抑制
study_object: 人类健康志愿者粪便样本，扩增子微生物组测序和短链脂肪酸测定
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are vital microbial metabolites that maintain gut health and immune function. Despite the established deleterious effect of antibiotics on anaerobic bacteria in the gut, the longitudinal effects of antibiotics on SCFA pool dynamics remain poorly characterized in humans. This study aimed to characterize depletion and recovery of linear and branched SCFAs and to explore microbial taxa associated with changes to SCFA pools after antibiotic exposure. This was a secondary analysis of a phase 1, randomized, nonblinded clinical trial in young healthy volunteers given a 10-day course of oral vancomycin, omadacycline, or moxifloxacin. Fecal samples were collected at baseline, during antibiotics, and follow-up visits for SCFA determinations and amplicon-based microbiome characterizations. Mixed effects models demonstrated that vancomycin produced global suppression of SCFAs pool relative to baseline, indicating broad suppression of microbial fermentation. Although all antibiotics reduced SCFA levels during treatment, vancomycin associated changes were most evident for branched SCFAs vs. comparators. Vancomycin shifted the fermentation balance by disproportionately suppressing linear SCFAs, reflected by a lower linear-to-branched SCFA ratio. In parallel, Clostridiales abundance declined most markedly after vancomycin, with more moderate reductions after omadacycline and moxifloxacin. Moxifloxacin and omadacycline but not vancomycin showed early recovery of butyrate-production capacity by qPCR. In this longitudinal analysis of healthy volunteers, vancomycin caused global suppression of microbial fermentation, with marked depletion of linear and branched SCFAs consistent with disproportionate suppression of fiber fermentation relative to amino acid fermentation.

title: Fecal microbiota transplantation in cancer immunotherapy: targeting the Gut-Tumor Axis.
authors: Yu Yue; Xu Caihua; Hua Yulin; Yang Fulin; Xie Shichang et al.
summary_zh: 综述评估粪菌移植在癌症免疫治疗中的临床证据，探讨供受体互作、微生物定植与宿主免疫及肿瘤背景对疗效和毒性的影响。
innovation: 提出“肠-肿瘤轴”框架整合微生物代谢物、细胞组分、跨器官免疫信号及瘤内微生物 | 强调多组学与计算建模用于可预测的精准微生物干预
limitation: 临床反应不一致 | 微生物组重塑不能可靠预测获益
study_object: 癌症患者/肠道/粪菌移植与免疫检查点抑制剂（综述）
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy, but resistance and immune-related toxicities continue to limit their benefit. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) may enhance ICI efficacy and alleviate treatment-related intestinal toxicity, yet clinical responses remain inconsistent, and microbiome remodeling does not reliably predict benefit. Moreover, clinical, ecological, and mechanistic evidence remains fragmented and has not been critically integrated. This review therefore evaluates the current clinical evidence for FMT in cancer immunotherapy and examines how donor-recipient interactions, microbial engraftment and function, host immunity, and tumor context jointly shape efficacy and toxicity. We organize these mechanisms within the Gut-Tumor Axis, encompassing microbial metabolites and cellular components, cross-organ immune signaling, and intratumoral microbiota. Finally, we discuss how multi-omics and computational modeling may enable more predictable and precise microbiome interventions.

title: Deep longitudinal phenotyping of a single individual enables host-microbiome metabolic modeling over 3.6 years.
authors: Sheehy Anna; Martinelli Filippo; Fang Xin; Smarr Larry; Palsson Bernhard O et al.
summary_zh: 对单一个体3.6年51个时间点的粪便宏基因组进行代谢建模，揭示大肠杆菌等驱动炎症的代谢机制。
innovation: 将时间点特异性微生物组模型与个性化全身代谢模型整合进行宿主-微生物组代谢建模 | 采用n-of-1纵向多组学设计解析微生物组动态与炎症的关系
limitation: 仅基于单一个体（n-of-1），结果普适性有限
study_object: 人类/肠道/粪便宏基因组测序与代谢建模
abstract: This study examines a single subject (LS) experiencing severe episodic colonic inflammation and associated gut microbiome dysbiosis. Metagenomic sequencing of LS's stool samples at 51 time points over 3.6 years provided a time series of gut microbial species' relative abundances, from which we generated time-point specific microbiome models. Flux balance analysis was used to predict metabolic phenotypes across the time series. The microbial abundances and predicted fluxes were compared with clinical inflammation biomarkers [serum C-reactive protein (CRP); stool lactoferrin, calprotectin, lysozyme, and secretory immunoglobulin A]. Each of these 51 microbiome models were integrated with a time-point specific male whole-body metabolic model personalized based on LS's weight, blood glucose, and cholesterol. A healthy average (HeAve) community model from 34 individuals provided a reference. Our models predicted methane overproduction from high Methanobrevibacter smithii levels, coinciding with peak CRP and calprotectin. We found that Escherichia coli plays a central role in shaping the predicted metabolome and may promote inflammation through trimethylamine N-oxide and formaldehyde production, out-competing Desulfovibrio piger and Akkermansia muciniphila via active methyl and sulfur cycles. At a later time point, LS experienced a major shift in gut Proteobacteria ecology: E. coli, over-abundant at 675 × HeAve, dropped nearly 80-fold in one month, while Morganella morganii rose by nearly eight times, which coincided with a spike in LS's lactoferrin and lysozyme, a rise in species including Klebsiella pneumoniae and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, a change in predicted metabolic profile, and increased alpha diversity. We also noted a correlation between postulated inflammation periods and predicted lithocholic acid levels. This work extends two previous studies of 7 and 27 of these time points. Our analysis demonstrates the value of pairing multi-omics time-series data with systems biology approaches in an n-of-1 design, resolving how microbiome composition dynamics shape host-microbiome metabolism and inflammation.

title: Fungal lignocellulose-degradation potential is associated with bacterial metabolic dysbiosis in the human gut.
authors: Liu Fei; Liu Ming-Yue; Zeng Zhao-Qing; Zhuang Wen-Ying; Cao Bin et al.
summary_zh: 通过实验和机器学习鉴定真菌木质纤维素降解基因特征，并分析其与人类肠道疾病及细菌代谢失调的关联。
innovation: 整合功能注释、同源群存在-缺失变异和机器学习模型，识别出优于传统注释的木质纤维素降解相关基因组特征 | 构建了非冗余的木质纤维素降解相关基因目录（LDAGs），涵盖典型降解酶、表型相关特征和候选同源群 | 将真菌基因组特征与细菌代谢失调及疾病状态（ACVD、IBD、肥胖）联系起来
limitation: 肥胖队列中LDAG总丰度差异在严格重映射标准下减弱 | 组成差异效应量较小
study_object: 人类肠道 + 真菌基因组和宏基因组 + 基因组-表型分析及机器学习
disease: 动脉粥样硬化性心血管疾病（ACVD）、炎症性肠病（IBD）、肥胖
sample_size: 762个环境真菌分离株；170个代表性菌株测序；160个基因组用于分析；2,116个公共真菌基因组；704个肠道真菌基因组；约1,500个人类肠道宏基因组
abstract: Fungi encode diverse carbohydrate-processing functions, yet the genomic basis of their lignocellulose-degradation potential and its relevance to the human gut remain poorly understood. Here, we experimentally assessed cellulase-, xylanase-, and laccase-associated activities across 762 environmentally derived fungal isolates and sequenced 170 representative strains, retaining 160 genomes for genome-phenotype analyses. By integrating functional annotations with orthogroup presence-absence variation and machine-learning models, we identified lignocellulose-degradation-associated genomic features that improved phenotype prediction beyond conventional annotation alone. We then applied this framework to 2,116 publicly available fungal genomes and 704 cultivated gut fungal genomes from a previously published collection to construct a non-redundant catalogue of lignocellulose-degradation-associated genes (LDAGs), comprising canonical degradative enzymes, annotated phenotype-associated features, and candidate orthogroups. Across fungal lineages, xylanase-associated potential was broadly distributed, cellulase-associated potential showed an intermediate pattern, whereas laccase-associated oxidative potential was concentrated in a more restricted subset of taxa. Analysis of approximately 1,500 publicly available human gut metagenomes identified disease-associated differences in LDAG profiles in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ACVD), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), and obesity. Under stringent read-remapping criteria, total LDAG abundance differences remained significant in ACVD and IBD but were attenuated in obesity, whereas compositional differences persisted across all three cohorts with modest effect sizes. These fungal genomic signatures covaried with bacterial taxa, including Escherichia coli, and pathways involved in central carbon and carbohydrate metabolism. Together, our findings establish a phenotype-informed genomic framework for resolving fungal lignocellulose-degradation potential and reveal its consistent association with disease-related bacterial and metabolic configurations in the human gut.

title: Bidirectional Interplay Between the Skin Microbiota and the Host: An EAACI Task Force Report.
authors: Callewaert Chris; Spacova Irina; Minnebo Yorick; De Pessemier Britta; De Muynck Magali et al.
summary_zh: 综述探讨皮肤微生物群与宿主内在因素的双向互作，及其对皮肤健康与疾病的影响。
innovation: 聚焦宿主内在因素（年龄、性别、激素、免疫及多组学）与皮肤微生物群的互作 | 系统讨论靶向皮肤微生物群的生物制剂和噬菌体疗法 | 指出当前知识空白以指导未来研究
study_object: 人类皮肤微生物组（细菌、真菌、古菌、病毒）
abstract: The skin microbiome is a diverse community of bacteria, fungi, archaea, and viruses colonizing the human skin and is thought to play an important role in skin health. Skin homeostasis and immunity are influenced by a dynamic interplay between the host immune system, the skin microbiome, and other host factors. Disruption of the skin microbiome well-functioning by environmental, lifestyle, and host-related factors can lead to dysbiosis, which has been associated to some pathological skin conditions, resulting in skin inflammation and an impaired barrier function. Building on the previous work from the EAACI Task Force that emphasized how environmental and lifestyle factors impact host resilience through the skin microbiome, the present review focuses on intrinsic host factors. We provide a comprehensive discussion on how the skin composition differs at different anatomical locations and is influenced by age, gender, hormones, immune system activity, and how the host "multi-omes" (genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome) interact with the skin microbiome. Additionally, we review current strategies to modify skin microbiome functions, including the role of diseases and medication, as well as topical microbiome-targeting biotic and bacteriophage therapies. Overall, this review highlights current knowledge and key research gaps, offering insights to guide future investigations and therapeutic innovations in skin health.

title: Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide-induced redox imbalance.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
authors: Hanna David A; Kumar Roshan; Ji Yuanyuan; Wong Harrison K A; Lyssiotis Costas A et al.
summary_zh: 慢性低水平硫化氢通过重塑氧化还原和核苷酸代谢，驱动多种人细胞系脂滴碳封存，以缓冲硫化氢诱导的氧化还原失衡。
innovation: 揭示硫化氢-脂滴-氧化还原轴 | 发现脂滴在应激响应中的主动作用 | 将微生物来源硫化氢与代谢健康联系起来
study_object: 人细胞系 + 未描述 + 未描述
abstract: The electron transport chain is a signaling hub for hydrogen sulfide (H2S) that serves both as a respiratory substrate and an inhibitor. While acute sulfide toxicity is well characterized, cellular adaptations to chronic H2S, particularly microbially-derived sulfide exposure in colon, is poorly understood. We report that chronic, low-level H2S exposure (4 to 20 µM) drives robust carbon sequestration in lipid droplets (LD) across several human cell lines, driven by a coordinated remodeling of redox and nucleotide metabolism. Specifically, H2S-induced reductive shifts in nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and coenzyme Q (CoQ) pools are accompanied by glycerol-3-phosphate accumulation and cytidine triphosphate (CTP) depletion. Lipidomic analysis reveals increased neutral lipid synthesis and triacylglyceride accumulation concomitant with decreased CTP-dependent synthesis of membrane phospholipids. Mitochondrial expression of a water-generating NADH oxidase attenuates LD accumulation and spatially confines the origin of H2S-induced reductive stress signaling to this compartment. Interestingly, LD abundance increases even after H2S withdrawal, continuing over 48 h, during which time the reductively-shifted NAD and CoQ pools slowly reoxidize. Inhibition of fatty acid synthesis during sulfide exposure impairs cellular recovery of respiration. These findings establish an active role for LDs in stress response and reveal that lipid biogenesis is a strategy for countering H2S-induced redox imbalance. The sulfide-LD-redox axis uncovered in this study has implications for understanding how gut-derived H2S, shaped by diet and microbiome, can influence metabolic health.

title: Gut microbiome and metabolomics reveal the role of thioproline in attenuating colorectal cancer-associated inflammation.
authors: Liu Jingjing; Li Wenchao; Qi Mingyang; Zhao Jian; Wu Jing et al.
summary_zh: 本研究通过宏基因组和代谢组学分析，发现硫脯氨酸可恢复结直肠癌小鼠肠道菌群组成及代谢物水平，提升亚油酸并减轻炎症。
innovation: 首次揭示硫脯氨酸通过调节肠道菌群和细菌代谢缓解结直肠癌相关炎症 | 整合宏基因组与代谢组学发现硫脯氨酸重塑微生物-代谢物互作网络并提升亚油酸水平
study_object: 小鼠/粪便和肠道组织/宏基因组与代谢组学
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the top three cancers globally in terms of both incidence and mortality, and its development may be influenced by an inflammatory environment in the intestines, often associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis. Food bioactives could modulate gut microbiota through anti-inflammatory and epigenetic mechanisms. Given the significant role of thioproline as a food bioactive with antioxidant properties, its potential to modulate gut microbiota and mitigate CRC remains largely unexplored. This study aims to understand the effects of thioproline on gut microbiota community and investigate the mechanisms through which thioproline regulates gut microbiota and exerts its anticancer effects. Fecal and intestinal tissue samples were collected from health, CRC, and thioproline-treated CRC mice. The metagenome and metabolome data revealed that thioproline treatment significantly altered the gut microbiota community composition and metabolism in CRC mice. These CRC-associated gut microbiota and bacterial metabolites returned to normal levels. Moreover, under thioproline treatment, the microbial-metabolite interactions in CRC mice shifted toward patterns more closely resembling those observed in healthy mice. Thioproline treatment increased linoleic acid levels in mice, indicating its role in promoting linoleic acid metabolism to therapeutically restore homeostasis and alleviate inflammation in CRC. This was further supported by hematoxylin and eosin staining, which demonstrated that thioproline alleviated inflammation in CRC mice. Our study highlights thioproline's dual role in regulating the gut microbiota community and bacterial metabolism, modulating bacteria-host interactions, and ultimately reducing inflammation in CRC. These findings offer valuable insights for future research and therapeutic applications.IMPORTANCEColorectal cancer (CRC) is associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis and intestinal inflammation. While food bioactives can modulate the microbiome, whether thioproline exerts inhibitory effects against CRC through microbial regulation remains unknown. Using integrated metagenomics and metabolomics, we show that thioproline treatment restores the gut microbiota composition and bacterial metabolites disrupted by CRC to near-normal levels. Importantly, thioproline remodels microbial metabolite interaction networks, elevates linoleic acid levels, and alleviates intestinal inflammation. This study provides a systems-level perspective on how a single dietary bioactive compound reshapes the gut microbial ecosystem and its metabolic landscape to reduce inflammation in CRC. Our findings suggest a potential role for microbiome-targeted nutritional strategies in protecting against CRC progression through modulation of the gut microbiota and intestinal microenvironment.

title: Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin is associated with delayed gut microbiome maturation in infants born to mothers with obesity.
authors: Kovenskiy Artur; Mukhanbetzhanov Nurislam; Jarmukhanov Zharkyn; Duisebayeva Arailym; Morenko Marina et al.
summary_zh: 本研究通过前瞻性纵向宏基因组测序，发现肥胖母亲婴儿肠道菌群成熟延迟，耐药基因负荷增加，大肠杆菌来源肠杆菌素与菌群成熟延迟相关。
innovation: 揭示母亲肥胖与婴儿肠道耐药组和毒力组功能变化的关联 | 发现大肠杆菌来源肠杆菌素可能通过铁清除机制促进肠杆菌科持久定植并延迟菌群成熟
limitation: 12个月时样本量最小，组间分类学差异不再具有统计学显著性
study_object: 婴儿/人类 + 粪便样本 + 鸟枪法宏基因组测序
abstract: Maternal obesity has been increasingly recognized as a factor influencing early-life microbiome development. However, its impact on the infant gut resistome and virulome remains insufficiently characterized. In this prospective longitudinal study, we investigated gut microbiome composition, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and virulence factor profiles in infants born to mothers with obesity and normal weight during the first year of life. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed on maternal and infant fecal samples collected at birth and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Infants born to obese mothers exhibited delayed microbiome maturation characterized by early enrichment of Pseudomonadota, particularly Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, and reduced abundance of Bifidobacterium species. This compositional pattern was accompanied by a significantly higher ARG burden in early life, including enrichment of genes associated with antibiotic inactivation, efflux mechanisms, and β-lactam resistance. Although taxonomic differences between groups were no longer statistically detectable at the 12-month time point, where the sample size was smallest, functional disparities in the resistome persisted. Additionally, infants born to obese mothers demonstrated increased relative abundance of secretory virulence-associated genes and E. coli-derived enterobactin, suggesting enhanced iron-scavenging capacity and competitive potential of Enterobacteriaceae. Together, these findings suggest that maternal obesity is associated with altered early microbial ecological dynamics, promotes resistome expansion, and may delay transition toward a stable Bacteroidota- and Bacillota-dominated microbiome.IMPORTANCEThe first year of life is a critical window for gut microbiome development, during which early microbial disturbances may influence later health. This study shows that maternal obesity is associated not only with altered infant microbial succession but also with functional changes in the infant gut microbiome, including greater antibiotic resistance gene burden and enrichment of virulence-associated traits. The finding of increased Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin suggests that iron-scavenging mechanisms may help Enterobacteriaceae persist during early infancy and may contribute to delayed microbial maturation. By linking maternal obesity with infant microbiome development, resistome expansion, and virulence-related functions, this work provides new insight into how maternal metabolic status may shape early microbial ecology and potential microbiome-associated risks.

title: Japanese encephalitis virus infection reshapes the gut microbiome and induces colonic inflammation in neonatal mice.
authors: Satheesan Anirudh; Priyadarsani Akasmika; Basu Anirban
summary_zh: 研究日本脑炎病毒感染新生小鼠后肠道菌群变化及结肠炎症，发现菌群失调和短链脂肪酸减少，补充短链脂肪酸可延长生存。
innovation: 揭示JEV感染通过减少进食和全身炎症导致结肠菌群失调 | 提出短链脂肪酸补充作为调节菌群治疗急性病毒感染的策略
study_object: 小鼠/粪便和结肠/16S rRNA测序
abstract: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), a neurotropic flavivirus, predominantly causes severe infection in children, leading to neuropsychiatric complications. Given that the juvenile period is a transitional window for the gut microbiota to develop into a stable community profile, any alterations to the microbiota during infections can result in chronic inflammation. Therefore, we investigated changes in the gut microbiota of neonatal mice during the early and late stages of JEV infection. Postnatal day 10, BALB/c mice challenged with JEV succumbed to acute infection at 6 to 7 days post-infection. This severity was marked by a surge in systemic pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-6, and MCP-1) and reduced food intake. Fecal 16S rRNA V3-V4 sequencing revealed distinct β-diversity between mock and JEV-infected groups, with the dominant phyla being Firmicutes, Bacteroidota, and Proteobacteria. The relative abundance of these phyla shifted, with Firmicutes decreasing from ~63.7% (control) to ~39% (JEV), whereas Proteobacteria remained unchanged in JEV. The Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio decreased in JEV, along with a reduction in Lactobacillus. Simultaneously, altered mucosal secretion, reduced tight-junction protein ZO-1, increased pNF-κB, and cleaved caspase-3 together indicated colonic inflammation. Prediction of microbial pathways using PICRUSt2 suggested a reduction in specific pathways associated with beneficial secondary metabolites and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in JEV. Intragastric administration of the SCFA cocktail prolonged survival and delayed the onset of clinical signs and the inflammatory response. Our findings suggest that systemic inflammation and reduced feeding during an acute infection could result in colonic dysbiosis, reduced beneficial bacteria, and trigger inflammation. SCFAs displayed a transient therapeutic effect in JEV infection, highlighting the potential of gut microbiota modulation to manage acute viral infection.IMPORTANCEJapanese encephalitis remains a leading cause of viral encephalitis in children across the Asia-Pacific region, with new outbreaks driven by evolving demographic factors. The need for targeted therapies beyond existing supportive care underscores the need for new host-directed interventions. Our findings suggest that gut-brain axis interactions may play a role in acute viral infections, potentially amplifying disease severity through infection-driven reduction in feeding, increased cytokine production, and shifts in the gut microbiome. We propose that SCFA supplementation can serve as a microbiota-modulating strategy that offers a safe, translatable approach to managing inflammation and JEV outcomes in pediatric viral encephalitis. This could be utilized as a supplement along with supportive care in other flavivirus infections.

title: Fragment End Motif Analysis of Microbial Cell-Free DNA Improves Detection of Pathogens over Noise from Contaminants and Commensals.
authors: Zhang Haikun; Dominguez Eddie G; Junak Mary; Lauer Kate V; Werner Nicole L et al.
summary_zh: 对38份血浆样本进行深度宏基因组测序，分析微生物游离DNA片段末端基序，发现结合丰度可提高病原体检测准确性。
innovation: 首次分析富集单链DNA文库中微生物游离DNA的5'和3'末端基序 | 将末端基序与微生物丰度结合，提高病原体与背景噪声的区分度
limitation: 样本量较小（38份血浆样本，仅5例脓毒症患者）
study_object: 人类血浆样本，采用深度宏基因组测序和单链DNA文库制备技术
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Circulating plasma microbial DNA (mDNA) is a promising biomarker for sepsis, but its accuracy is hindered by the low abundance of pathogen DNA and the presence of contaminants and commensals. mDNA enrichment using a selection of short fragments and single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) library preparation can improve pathogen yield but also increases background noise. Since nucleotide representation at mDNA fragment ends is biased by enzymatic digestion in vivo, we hypothesized that analysis of 5' and 3' mDNA fragment end motifs in enriched ssDNA libraries could improve pathogen detection.
METHODS: We performed deep metagenomic sequencing of size-selected ssDNA libraries from 38 plasma samples, including 20 samples from 5 sepsis patients, 18 samples from 6 patients without infection, and 6 no-template controls. Across these samples, we compared observed-to-expected ratios for end motifs in mDNA fragments from candidate pathogens and contaminants. For each candidate pathogen, we evaluated the accuracy of combining end motifs with microbial abundance for detection of infection.
RESULTS: mDNA fragments from infection-causing pathogens were biased in the nucleotide motifs at both fragment ends compared with contaminants, with the highest enrichment observed in the GG dinucleotide at the 3' end (P < 0.0001). Integrating microbial abundance with end motif features improved differentiation between clinically significant pathogens and corresponding noise from the same microbes in noninfection samples. For Staphylococcus infections, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for the combination model was higher than than that for microbial abundance alone (0.892 vs 0.431, respectively; P = 0.018).
CONCLUSIONS: mDNA end motif analysis improves signal-to-noise ratio beyond microbial abundance alone and improves pathogen detection in plasma metagenomic sequencing.

title: Oral exposure to perfluorooctanoic acid disrupts the microbiota-gut-liver axis and enhances the severity of chemically induced colitis in mice.
authors: Park Jungjae; Miller Alessandra S; Pore Gatha; Banginwar Maithili; Lee Sarah et al.
summary_zh: 小鼠口服PFOA暴露改变肠道通透性、菌群和胆汁酸，加重DSS诱导的雄性小鼠结肠炎。
innovation: 揭示早期生命口服PFOA暴露通过破坏肠-肝轴加重化学诱导结肠炎 | 发现PFOA加重结肠炎具有性别依赖性（仅雄性小鼠）
study_object: 小鼠/肠道、肝脏/16S测序、生理病理及胆汁酸检测
disease: 炎症性肠病（IBD）、DSS诱导结肠炎
abstract: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) affect millions of patients worldwide and impair quality of life. Although genetic and environmental factors are known to disrupt the gastrointestinal (GI) epithelial barrier and increase susceptibility to IBD, the precise contribution of specific environmental exposures remains unclear. Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), or "forever chemicals," are widely used in consumer products and contaminate food and water sources, resulting in chronic oral exposure worldwide. Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a common PFAS, has been epidemiologically associated with the development of IBD, particularly in older adults. Here, we assessed the effects of oral PFOA exposure on the GI tract, liver, and susceptibility to colitis. C57BL/6 mice were exposed to PFOA (0.1 or 1.0 mg/kg) beginning at weaning (postnatal day [P]21) for a time course of 4 or 8 weeks. GI physiology/pathology (Ussing chambers; histology), expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (qPCR), microbiota composition (16S sequencing), bile acid production (qPCR; LC/MS), and liver pathology (histology) were assessed. Colitis susceptibility was evaluated in genetically predisposed (IL10 knockout) mice, and in chemically induced (dextran sodium sulfate [DSS]) mouse models following PFOA exposure (8 weeks at 1.0 mg/kg). Oral PFOA exposure increased intestinal permeability, mildly increased cytokine expression, altered gut microbiota composition, disrupted liver and serum bile acids, and caused hepatic hypertrophy in the high dose and longer exposure. Although PFOA did not increase disease susceptibility in genetically predisposed IL10 KO mice, it significantly worsened DSS-induced colitis, but only in male mice. Together, these findings demonstrate that early-life PFOA exposure disrupts the gut-liver axis and may contribute to colitis development in a sex-dependent manner.

title: Characterizing gut microbial structural variation reveals strain heterogeneity and metabolic dysfunction in colorectal cancer.
authors: Cui Ying; Qiu Qintian; Chen Yongqiu; Ding Tao
summary_zh: 分析1027份粪便宏基因组，鉴定细菌结构变异，发现其可区分结直肠癌与健康人并关联代谢紊乱。
innovation: 首次系统刻画结直肠癌相关肠道微生物结构变异图谱 | 整合分类与结构变异标记提升早期结直肠癌检测准确性 | 开发MicroSVsProfiler框架识别和分类结构变异
limitation: 未来需探索不同阶段结直肠癌的结构变异组 | 未描述
study_object: 人类/肠道/粪便宏基因组
abstract: Previous studies investigating gastrointestinal (GI) diseases have primarily focused on the composition, gene expression, and specific strains of gut microbiota. However, the impact of genetic variations, especially structural variations (SVs) in microbial genomes, on the development of GI tumors has been largely overlooked. In this study, we analyzed 1,027 fecal metagenomes from seven data sets and identified 8,278 coverage-defined SVs across 51 bacterial species in the gut microbiomes. We found that SVs were prevalent in the gut microbiota of studied cohorts. Surprisingly, the genetic makeup of SV-based clusters differed significantly between healthy individuals and those with colorectal cancer (CRC), indicating substantial intra-specific diversity within these populations. By integrating taxonomic-SV markers, we achieved optimal accuracy in early CRC detection, and the SVs also displayed regional heterogeneity. Microbial genetic variation provides additional insights into taxonomy and functionality, allowing us to have a more precise understanding of the microbiota associated with CRC. Notably, our study uncovered potential links between microbial SVs and metabolic disorders of CRC, including SV regions that encode glycoside hydrolases associated with disordered carbohydrate metabolism in CRC. We integrated a framework called MicroSVsProfiler to identify and classify SVs in individuals diagnosed with CRC, as well as in healthy controls. Our findings underscore the importance of considering SVs in microbiome studies, especially in the absence of strain-specific differences in abundance. Future research should explore the deeper layer of the microbiota's structural variantome for a better understanding of the occurrence and characteristics of CRC across different stages.IMPORTANCEMost microbiome studies of colorectal cancer focus on which bacterial species are more or less abundant, potentially overlooking genetic differences among strains of the same species. By analyzing 1,027 fecal metagenomes from seven independent cohorts, we show that large-scale changes in bacterial genomes, known as structural variations, provide disease-related information that is not captured by species abundance alone. These strain-level SV signatures distinguished healthy individuals from patients with colorectal cancer, improved early-cancer classification when combined with taxonomic markers, and varied across geographic populations. We also found that cancer-associated structural variations were linked to altered microbial metabolic functions, particularly carbohydrate metabolism and glycoside hydrolases. Together, these findings establish microbial structural variation as a complementary dimension of the gut microbiome and provide a framework for developing more precise, population-aware biomarkers and for investigating how strain-level genetic changes may contribute to metabolic disturbances associated with colorectal cancer.

title: Network pharmacology, gut microbiota, and metabolomics integration reveal that Shenshuai 'an enema prescription (SSAEP) improves CRF mechanisms by reshaping the gut microbiota and correcting host-microbe cometabolism.
authors: Liu Shilin; Li Andong; Jia Ailing; Chen Qiang; Nan Zheng et al.
summary_zh: 本研究结合网络药理学、16S rRNA测序和代谢组学，揭示肾衰安灌肠方通过重塑肠道菌群、纠正宿主-微生物共代谢紊乱改善慢性肾衰竭大鼠的作用机制。
innovation: 从间接药理学角度系统阐释SSAEP通过肠-肾轴改善CRF的机制 | 整合网络药理学、16S rRNA测序和代谢组学多学科方法 | 通过抗生素干预和粪菌移植实验验证肠道菌群的关键介导作用
study_object: 大鼠/慢性肾衰竭模型+血清和结肠内容物+16S rRNA基因测序和代谢组学
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic renal failure (CRF) is a global health issue, and the "gut-kidney axis" plays a key role in its pathogenesis. Shenshuai 'an enema prescription (SSAEP) is a Chinese medicine compound based on the TCM theory of "regulation of bowel movement and removal of turbid qi", which has shown good adjunctive therapeutic effects in delaying the progression of CRF in clinical practice. However, its specific mechanisms remain unclear.
PURPOSE: Herein, from the perspective of indirect pharmacology, the therapeutic effects of SSAEP on CRF rats were explored. We hypothesize that its mechanism of action may be largely indirect and occurs primarily through the gut-kidney axis. This study aimed to systematically elucidate the potential mechanism through which SSAEP improves CRF through the regulation of gut microecology using multidisciplinary approaches such as network pharmacology, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and metabonomics.
METHODS: A CRF rat model was established by induction with 2.5% adenine. Low and high doses of SSAEP were administered via enema, and antibiotic intervention and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) experiments were performed to verify the key mediating role of the gut microbiota. The chemical composition of the SSAEP and the metabolic profiles of the serum and colonic contents of the rats were analyzed using UHPLC‒MS/MS; the composition of the gut microbiota was analyzed through 16S rRNA sequencing; and the core targets and pathways were predicted using network pharmacology and molecular docking. In vitro, human renal tubular epithelial cells (HK-2) were stimulated with TGF-β1 or glycochenodeoxycholic acid (GCDCA) to verify the anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic effects of quercetin (the main active component of SSAEP) and the role of the IL-17 signaling pathway in this process.
RESULTS: SSAEP treatment significantly improved renal function indicators (BUN, SCR, Cys-C, and UA) in CRF rats and alleviated pathological damage, the inflammatory response, and fibrosis in kidney tissue. Antibiotic intervention attenuated the protective effect of SSAEP, while FMT experiments confirmed that the efficacy of SSAEP could be transferred to recipient rats through the transplantation of treated fecal microbiota. SSAEP reshaped the gut microbiota, significantly increasing the abundance of Akkermansia while reducing that of Clostridium. Metabolomic analysis revealed CRF-related metabolic disturbances and identified 29 key differentially expressed metabolites regulated by SSAEP, among which glycochenodeoxycholic acid (GCDCA) was a key pathogenic metabolite. Network pharmacology predictions combined with in vitro experiments confirmed that the quercetin in SSAEP could effectively antagonize the TGF-β1- and GCDCA-induced epithelial‒mesenchymal transition and inflammatory response in HK-2 cells by inhibiting the IL-17/NF-κB signaling pathway.
CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that SSAEP improves CRF through an indirect pharmacological mechanism dependent on the gut microbiota: SSAEP reshapes the balance of the gut microbiota, thereby correcting host-microbe cometabolic disorders (particularly by reducing the level of the pathogenic metabolite GCDCA) and ultimately alleviating renal inflammation and fibrosis through the inhibition of signaling pathways such as the IL-17/NF-κB pathway. This study provides new experimental evidence for the "gut-kidney axis" theory and lays the foundation for the development of CRF treatment strategies based on the regulation of the gut microbiome.

title: Amino acid-based formula and Clostridioides difficile-associated disease in infants: concerns regarding causal interpretation.
authors: Jiang Xun; Wang Ying; Luo Youyou; Jin Cuiyuan; Zeng Zhaoyang et al.
summary_zh: 指出氨基酸配方喂养与婴儿艰难梭菌关联病的研究存在因果推断局限，建议仅视为关联而非因果。
innovation: 系统梳理了从关联到因果推断的证据缺口 | 提出了决定性前瞻性研究的具体要素
limitation: 多变量模型仅27个结局事件，事件每变量约4.5，远低于10-20阈值 | 横断面微生物组数据无法确定微生物改变与疾病的先后关系
study_object: 婴儿/儿童 + 粪便 + 微生物组分析与粪菌移植实验
abstract: Wang et al. recently reported an association between amino acid-based formula (AAF) feeding and Clostridioides difficile-associated disease (CDAD) in children younger than two years, integrating clinical observations, microbiome profiling, and fecal microbiota transplantation experiments. The authors appropriately framed their findings as associative; our aim is not to allege over-interpretation, but to delineate the evidentiary gap between their reported association and a causal claim. Several methodological and interpretative issues limit such inference, including confounding by the clinical indication for AAF, the difficulty of distinguishing C. difficile colonization from clinically attributable disease in young children, developmental differences in age and complementary feeding, and the selected nature of the fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) donor population. For example, the multivariable model included only 27 outcome events against approximately six predictors (events-per-variable ≈ 4.5, far below the accepted 10-20 threshold), rendering the adjusted odds ratios unstable. The cross-sectional microbiome data further cannot establish whether microbial alterations preceded disease or resulted from underlying clinical, dietary, or inflammatory states. We therefore suggest interpreting the findings as an association between AAF feeding and CDAD status, rather than evidence that AAF itself increases CDAD risk. Our skepticism concerns the causal link to CDAD specifically; we do not dispute that reduced Bifidobacterium with formula feeding is a well-established finding. This distinction has important clinical implications, as AAF remains an essential nutritional intervention for children with appropriate indications, and in young children microbiological detection and microbiome alterations must be interpreted alongside age, clinical symptoms, underlying disease, dietary history, and other relevant exposures. An overly causal interpretation could create unnecessary concern among families and complicate clinical decision-making. To make these considerations operational, we specify the elements of a decisive prospective study, including a minimum event count of ~60 adjudicated CDAD cases, a blinded tiered diagnostic algorithm, and detailed AAF exposure ascertainment.

title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis and associated metabolome changes in tuberculosis patients resolve partially post-therapy.
authors: Sahu Sukanya; Kaushik Sandeep R; Chaudhary Shweta; Mohapatra Amit Kumar; Kupa Rukuwe-U et al.
summary_zh: 分析活动性结核患者粪便菌群与代谢物，发现菌群失调并在治疗后部分恢复。
innovation: 结合16S rRNA测序与GC-TOF-MS分析结核患者肠道菌群与代谢物关联 | 纵向随访揭示抗结核治疗中菌群和代谢物的动态变化
limitation: 纵向随访队列样本量小（n=10）
study_object: 人类/肠道/粪便/16S rRNA测序与GC-TOF-MS代谢组学
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection in the host and subsequent treatment with anti-tuberculosis drugs impact lung pathophysiology and influence the lung and gut microbiome. Elucidating the role of the gut microbiome and its metabolites in the perturbed metabolic and immune functions observed in tuberculosis (TB) might help design corrective prebiotic and probiotic mixtures.
METHODOLOGY: In this study, fecal samples (n = 107) of drug-naïve active TB patients (ATB) and controls (other respiratory disease: NTB and healthy) from the two clinical sites were analyzed for microbiota composition (16S rRNA sequencing), metabolites (GC-TOF-MS), and their correlation. In addition, a longitudinal follow-up study was conducted to understand the dynamics of the microbiota and metabolites during anti-TB treatment in a small cohort (n = 10).
RESULTS: Gut microbiota showed site-specificity; however, an overall reduction in alpha diversity was observed in disease states compared with healthy subjects. Underrepresentation of gut commensals (Faecalibacterium, Ligilactobacillus and Romboustia) and overrepresentation of Thomasclavelia and Clostridioides were observed among active TB patients. The longitudinally followed-up ATB subjects undergoing treatment showed a time-dependent increase in beta-diversity variance. Over time, the beta diversity of follow-up subjects was almost similar to that of healthy controls. Decrease in the abundance of Streptococcus occurred after anti-TB treatment, with higher levels of opportunistic pathogens, such as Escherichia and Stenotrophomonas. Similarly, specific fecal metabolites also returned to pretreatment levels in relative abundance at later time points.
CONCLUSIONS: The gut microbiota of TB patients showed dysbiosis at the time of case presentation and partially resolved upon complete therapeutic interventions. Partial recovery of microbiota observed during treatment is also reflected in the fecal metabolome, indicating the possible use of microbiome and metabolites as adjunct therapeutics in TB.

title: The BspC surface adhesin and gastrointestinal fungal colonization enhance group B streptococcal neonatal infection.
authors: Crossen Arianne J; Cohen Shirli; Manzer Haider S; Zackular Joseph P; Ost Kyla S et al.
summary_zh: 研究揭示BspC黏附素和真菌定植促进B族链球菌肠道定植及新生儿感染。
innovation: 发现ST-17相关表面黏附素BspC介导GBS肠道上皮黏附和全身播散 | 证明白色念珠菌以BspC依赖方式增强GBS肠道黏附和脑部播散 | 结合人类婴儿粪便微生物组数据验证念珠菌定植与GBS丰度正相关
study_object: 新生儿小鼠/人类婴儿 + 肠道/粪便 + 动物模型/细胞模型/微生物组分析
disease: 新生儿败血症、肺炎、脑膜炎
abstract: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) colonizes the gastrointestinal (GI) and female reproductive tracts of up to 30% of healthy adults, but during pregnancy can be transmitted to the newborn, causing neonatal sepsis, pneumonia, and meningitis. Neonatal GI colonization is an important precursor to invasive disease, yet the mechanisms governing GBS intestinal persistence and dissemination are still being elucidated. Given the predominance of hypervirulent sequence type 17 (ST-17) strains in neonatal invasive disease, we hypothesized that the ST-17-associated surface adhesin BspC contributes to gastrointestinal colonization and infection. Using a neonatal mouse model, we found that pups infected with wild-type GBS exhibited increased mortality and significantly higher bacterial burdens in the intestine, blood, spleen, and brain compared with pups infected with a ΔbspC mutant. We also observed that BspC promoted adherence to a 2D organoid model of the human infant colon and Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells through its variable domain. Building on previous findings that Candida albicans interacts with BspC, we found that C. albicans enhanced GBS intestinal epithelial adherence in a BspC-dependent manner, and coinfection increased intestinal GBS burden and brain dissemination in neonatal mice. Finally, analysis of published human neonatal fecal microbiome data sets revealed higher GBS abundance in infants colonized with C. albicans or other Candida species. Together, these findings identify BspC as a key mediator of GBS intestinal colonization and invasive disease and suggest that fungal colonization of the neonatal GI promotes GBS pathogenesis.IMPORTANCEGroup B Streptococcus (GBS) is a leading cause of neonatal infection, which can result in fatality or long-term neurological morbidity in survivors. Intestinal colonization is an important precursor to invasive disease, yet the factors that promote GBS persistence in the neonatal gastrointestinal tract remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the GBS surface adhesin BspC as a mediator of intestinal epithelial adherence, gastrointestinal colonization, and systemic dissemination. We further demonstrate that the common fungal pathobiont Candida albicans enhances GBS intestinal adherence and infection. Consistent with our experimental findings, analysis of human infant microbiome data sets revealed greater GBS abundance in infants colonized with Candida species. These findings identify BspC as a key mediator of this process and suggest that fungal colonization can enhance GBS disease.

title: Whole-genome characterization and genomic stability of Mastadenovirus F40 and F41 in pediatric gastroenteritis.
authors: El-Shahidy Samar M; Zakaria Amira M; Ibrahim Mohanad A; Diab Atef M
summary_zh: 研究儿童急性胃肠炎中肠道腺病毒F40/F41的流行病学与基因组特征，通过PCR筛查和宏基因组测序分析5株病毒，发现高基因组保守性且无重组证据。
innovation: 对5株HAdV-F40/F41进行全基因组重建和全面基因组分析 | 结合基因特异性系统发育、序列一致性和全基因组比较验证分子分型可靠性 | 扩展了循环HAdV-F40/F41毒株的有限基因组数据
limitation: 仅对5株代表性阳性样本进行测序，样本量有限
study_object: 住院儿童粪便样本，采用多重胃肠道实时PCR和鸟枪法宏基因组测序
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Human adenovirus types 40 and 41 (HAdV-40 and HAdV-41), belonging to the species Mastadenovirus faecale, are among the leading viral causes of acute gastroenteritis in children. Despite their clinical importance, whole-genome data on circulating strains remain limited. This study investigated the epidemiological and genomic characteristics of enteric Mastadenoviruses detected in children with acute gastroenteritis.
METHODS: A total of 632 stool specimens collected from hospitalized children with acute gastroenteritis were screened using a multiplex gastrointestinal real-time PCR panel. Five representative Mastadenovirus-positive samples underwent shotgun metagenomic sequencing followed by genome reconstruction, phylogenetic analysis, pairwise sequence identity comparisons, genome-wide variant analysis, amino acid substitution profiling, and recombination analysis.
RESULTS: Mastadenoviruses were detected in 60/632 (9.5%) children, with the highest positivity observed among those aged 1-3 years. Co-infections occurred predominantly involving bacterial pathogens. Complete or near-complete genomes were recovered for all five sequenced isolates with high sequencing depth (2,806 × -34,120 ×), genome coverage (94.8%-100% at ≥ 10 ×), and nucleotide identity (99.19%-99.78%) relative to genotype-matched reference genomes. Phylogenetic analyses identified two HAdV-F40 and three HAdV-F41 isolates. Gene-specific phylogenies of the hexon, penton base, fiber, and DNA polymerase genes consistently confirmed genotype assignment. Pairwise sequence identity analysis and recombination analysis further supported classification with no evidence of intergenotypic recombination.
CONCLUSIONS: The sequenced enteric Mastadenovirus isolates exhibited high genomic conservation with limited within-genotype diversity and no detectable evidence of recent recombination. The concordance between gene-specific phylogenies, sequence identity analyses, and whole-genome comparisons supports the robustness of current molecular typing approaches and expands the limited genomic data available for circulating HAdV-F40 and HAdV-F41 strains.

title: Barrier-reinforcing hyaluronic acid-bilirubin nanodelivery of methylprednisolone for synergistic modulation of the intestinal barrier, immune system, and gut microbiome in colitis.
journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
authors: Lee Bom; Yoo Jeeeun; Jeon Hyeon-Jeong; Kim Yu Jeong; Cheng Xiaoliang et al.
summary_zh: 研究开发载甲泼尼龙透明质酸-胆红素纳米粒口服治疗结肠炎，在DSS模型中改善肠屏障并协同调节免疫与菌群。
innovation: 开发MPS@HABN口服纳米药物，保护肠上皮免受MPS损伤并增强低剂量HABN的免疫和菌群调节 | 实现低HABN剂量和临床相关MPS剂量下优于单组分的协同疗效
study_object: 小鼠/结肠炎模型+结肠组织+纳米药物与微生物组分析
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by a self-reinforcing cycle of intestinal barrier dysfunction, gut microbiome dysbiosis, and aberrant mucosal immune responses. Methylprednisolone (MPS) is a potent immunosuppressant used for IBD and may beneficially modulate the gut microbiome, but its systemic adverse effects and potential impairment of epithelial repair limit its therapeutic use. To overcome these limitations, we developed MPS-loaded hyaluronic acid-bilirubin nanoparticles (MPS@HABN), an oral nanomedicine designed to protect the intestinal epithelium from MPS-associated injury while enhancing the otherwise limited immune and microbiome modulation achieved by low-dose HABN. MPS@HABN limited premature drug release, increased MPS accumulation in the inflamed colon, and reduced systemic exposure and thymic involution. It also protected intestinal epithelial cells from MPS-associated and oxidative injury. In contrast, low-dose HABN alone showed limited immune and microbiome modulation, whereas free MPS caused intestinal barrier damage and systemic toxicity such as thymic involution. In a DSS-induced colitis model, MPS@HABN improved intestinal barrier function while enhancing immune and microbiome modulation, resulting in robust therapeutic efficacy beyond that of either component alone at a low HABN dose and a clinically relevant MPS dose. These findings support combining the complementary activities of MPS and HABN to overcome corticosteroid-associated epithelial injury and the limited efficacy of low-dose HABN, thereby helping to disrupt the pathological barrier-immune-microbiome cycle in colitis.

title: IBD is associated with species-specific changes in gut microbial gene diversity.
authors: Mazzoni Chiara; Yassour Moran
summary_zh: 通过宏基因组分析比较IBD患者与对照的肠道共生菌种内多样性，发现物种特异性基因多样性变化及运动、铁摄取相关功能差异。
innovation: 从菌株水平种群遗传多样性角度揭示IBD相关应激下的细菌动态 | 识别出在IBD应激下可能受选择的基因和功能（如运动、铁摄取）
study_object: 人类肠道菌群宏基因组
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Intra-species genomic variation provides the raw material for natural selection and can reflect the recent diversification history of microbial populations. Environmental stress may be regarded as the ultimate accelerator of the evolutionary process, especially for microorganisms, which can alter their DNA if presented with nutrient limitation, toxins, or pathogen attack. Chronic intestinal inflammation, as in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), represents prolonged environmental stress for gut commensal bacteria, bringing many enteric species down to undetectable levels. However, it remains unclear how microbes that colonize IBD patients actually respond to IBD-associated stressors and whether stress-driven bacterial dynamics may be identified at the population level from the bacterial gut metagenome. To investigate IBD-associated strain-level population dynamics, we performed metagenomic analyses focusing on measuring within-individual bacterial diversity for a panel of gut commensals present across IBD patients and Controls. First, we found species-specific differences in genome-level bacterial diversity. Then, we found that certain genes and functions may harbor different levels and kinds of genetic divergence within the same species across IBD patients and Controls. Functions that were enriched in IBD with both neutral divergence and functional divergence were associated with motility and iron-scavenging, among others. These results may point toward functions that are under selection in the context of IBD stress and could inform future mechanistic work, exploring previously unknown routes of bacterial diversification and adaptation to stress in the gut microbiome.
IMPORTANCE: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by profound alterations in the gut microbiome composition, and most research so far has focused on changes in species-level abundance to understand gut microbiome contributions to disease dynamics. However, investigating strain-level variation has the potential to uncover previously unknown factors underlying bacterial persistence during gut inflammation, hence revealing key aspects driving gut dysbiosis. Here, we showed that IBD is associated with species-specific changes in gut microbial population-level genetic diversity and identified individual genes and functions that seem to harbor differential genetic diversity within IBD-associated strains. More broadly, our results highlight how intra-species population- and gene-level diversity could be used as sensors of environmental stress in the gut microbiome, and further studies could follow up on the functions highlighted in this work to establish causal links between gut inflammatory conditions and processes of bacterial adaptation to stress.

title: Gut microbiome depletion aggravates glial-mediated Alzheimer's disease pathology through inflammatory, metabolic, and proteostatic dysregulation.
authors: Madamanchi Kishore; Gurrala Srinath; Watson John; Melkani Girish
summary_zh: 利用人源化果蝇AD模型，发现肠道菌群耗竭通过炎症、代谢和蛋白稳态失调加重胶质介导的AD病理及行为缺陷。
innovation: 使用表达人AD相关转基因的胶质细胞人源化果蝇模型研究肠-脑轴 | 通过抗生素实现肠道菌群显著耗竭并系统评估行为、生理和分子变化 | 揭示神经炎症与aβ42、pTau及APP积累之间的关联
study_object: 果蝇 + 肠道 + 人源化AD转基因模型 + 抗生素处理
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic neuroinflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and impaired proteostasis. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiome influences brain function through the gut-brain axis; however, the mechanisms by which this communication affects AD pathology remain poorly understood. In this study, we used humanized Drosophila AD models expressing human AD-related transgenes in glial cells to investigate how glial AD pathology influences the gut microbiome and how microbiome depletion affects behavior and disease progression. Our findings revealed significant alterations in the abundance of several gut microbial taxa, including Lactobacillus, Acetobacter, Enterococcus, Enterobacter, Pseudomonas, Leuconostoc, Providencia, and Gluconobacter, suggesting a potential interaction between the gut microbiome and AD progression. To further define the role of the gut microbiome in AD progression, we treated Drosophila with antibiotics to achieve substantial microbiome depletion (SMD) and evaluated the resulting behavioral, physiological, and molecular changes. Compared with conventional controls, flies with SMD exhibited enhanced inflammatory signaling and cell death, impaired autophagy, lipid dysregulation, and increased accumulation of amyloid β-42 (aβ42) and phospho-tau (pTau), with the extent of these changes varying among the different humanized AD models. These molecular alterations further exacerbated sleepcircadian disruption, altered locomotor performance, and worsened learning and memory deficits. Furthermore, we demonstrated a link between enhanced neuroinflammation and the accumulation of aβ42, pTau, and amyloid precursor protein (APP) proteins. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that gut microbiome depletion aggravates glial-mediated AD pathology through the coordinated disruption of inflammatory, metabolic, and proteostatic pathways, ultimately leading to behavioral dysfunction. These results identify the gut microbiome as a critical regulator of glial homeostasis and provide new insights into its contribution to the progression of neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Microbial and antimicrobial resistance signatures differentiate healthy and inflamed ileal pouches in patients with ulcerative colitis.
authors: Dall Sebastian Mølvang; Møllekær Alberte Holm; Kousgaard Sabrina Just; Jakobsen Sarah Søgaard; Larsen Lone et al.
summary_zh: 比较健康与炎症回肠储袋、溃疡性结肠炎及正常结肠的粪便微生物，发现健康储袋菌群独特，且大肠杆菌耐药突变与质粒相关。
innovation: 首次系统比较健康回肠储袋与慢性储袋炎、溃疡性结肠炎及正常结肠的微生物组差异 | 利用长读长测序重建MAGs并结合DNA甲基化进行质粒-宿主关联分析 | 揭示储袋炎中大肠杆菌gyrA和parC基因协同耐药突变及质粒携带的ESBL基因
study_object: 人类/粪便样本/Illumina和Oxford Nanopore测序
disease: 溃疡性结肠炎、慢性储袋炎、健康回肠储袋
sample_size: n=190（HealthyPouch n=38, SickPouch n=37, UC n=23, NormalGut n=92）
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) from healthy donors with a normally functioning colon has limited clinical effect in the treatment of chronic pouchitis. However, a normally functioning ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA) physiology differs from individuals with a healthy intact colon. We aimed to investigate the microbial characteristics of patients with a normally functioning IPAA (HealthyPouch) compared with chronic pouchitis (SickPouch), ulcerative colitis (UC), and a healthy intact colon microbiome (NormalGut). Furthermore, we investigated how repeated antibiotic use influences antimicrobial resistance on a bacterial genome level.
METHODS: Fecal samples from 190 participants were collected; HealthyPouch (n = 38), SickPouch (n = 37), UC (n = 23), and NormalGut (n = 92) and sequenced with Illumina and taxonomically profiled. Samples from HealthyPouch, SickPouch, and NormalGut were also long-read sequenced using Oxford Nanopore Technologies for reconstruction of 12 282 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). DNA methylation motifs were used for plasmid-host association.
RESULTS: The HealthyPouch microbiome is distinct from both the UC, NormalGut, and SickPouch microbiome. Escherichia coli MAGs in the SickPouch (n = 21) microbiome had significantly higher co-occurring ciprofloxacin resistance mutations in the gyrA and parC genes, compared to both HealthyPouch (n = 26; BH adjusted P < .05) and NormalGut (n = 40; BH adjusted P < .05). Based on DNA methylation pattern, three plasmids were associated with E. coli carrying extended-spectrum beta lactamase genes.
CONCLUSIONS: HealthyPouch microbiota differs from NormalGut microbiota, and could therefore be more appropriate for FMT treatment of chronic pouchitis. The association between E. coli and resistance gene-carrying plasmids underscores the importance of integrating plasmid analysis into metagenome-based approaches for personalized antibiotic treatment and resistance monitoring.

title: Antibiotic Exposure and Treatment Outcomes in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Psyllia Dimitra; Stylianakis Dimitrios; Denaro Nerina; Pistis Marco; Lambertini Matteo et al.
summary_zh: 系统评价与荟萃分析显示，头颈鳞癌和鼻咽癌治疗前后全身抗生素暴露与更差生存和反应相关。
innovation: 综合评估抗生素暴露在ICI和CRT治疗中的预后关联 | 分别分析不同时间窗抗生素暴露与生存结局的关系
limitation: 证据以观察性研究为主，存在显著适应证混杂，无法推断因果 | 多数研究存在严重/高偏倚风险
study_object: 头颈鳞状细胞癌和鼻咽癌患者 + 全身抗生素暴露 + 系统评价与荟萃分析
disease: 头颈鳞状细胞癌、鼻咽癌
abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Systemic antibiotics may disrupt the gut and oral microbiome, potentially affecting anticancer treatment efficacy. Their prognostic relevance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), particularly during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapy or definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT), remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated associations between systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation and oncologic outcomes.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from January 2015 to March 28, 2026. Eligible studies included patients with HNSCC or NPC receiving ICI, definitive CRT, or chemo-immunotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), or objective response rate (ORR). Random-effects models pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for OS and PFS; ORR was synthesized descriptively. Risk of bias was assessed, as appropriate, using ROBINS-I, ROBINS-E, RoB 2, or the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.
RESULTS: Eleven studies involving 6,293 patients were included; nine studies (4,507 patients) contributed to survival meta-analyses. Antibiotic exposure was associated with worse OS (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.52-2.08) and PFS (HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.28-1.96). Associations were consistent in ICI-treated cohorts (OS HR 1.80, 95% CI 1.53-2.13; PFS HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.24-2.25) and CRT cohorts (OS HR 1.73, 95% CI 1.29-2.32; PFS HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.11-2.11). Heterogeneity was low-to-moderate for OS (I2=28.6%) and negligible for PFS (I2=0%). Leave-one-out analyses showed stable OS (HR range 1.76-1.86) and PFS estimates (1.58-1.63). Worse OS was observed for both 30-60-day pre-ICI exposure (HR 2.04, 95% CI 1.43-2.90) and concurrent/peri-treatment exposure (HR 1.74, 95% CI 1.49-2.04). ORR was descriptively lower in antibiotic-exposed patients. Most studies had serious/high risk of bias, primarily due to confounding by indication.
CONCLUSIONS: Systemic antibiotic exposure around treatment initiation is associated with inferior survival and response in HNSCC and NPC. However, predominantly observational evidence and substantial confounding preclude causal inference. Prospective microbiome-informed studies are needed.

title: Bacteriophage-Derived Endolysins in Atopic Dermatitis and Other Pruritic Dermatoses: Mechanistic Rationale, Clinical Evidence, and Limitations.
authors: Farhadi Leah; Khalil Nicole; Kowalczyk Wiktoria; Lio Peter; Yosipovitch Gil
summary_zh: 综述噬菌体衍生内溶素靶向清除金黄色葡萄球菌治疗特应性皮炎瘙痒的机制、临床证据及局限。
innovation: 提出内溶素作为比广谱抗菌药更靶向的微生物组导向疗法 | 系统整合内溶素作用机制、临床证据与配方/患者选择等未解问题
limitation: 早期特应性皮炎临床证据不一致 | 配方、患者选择、细菌快速裂解所致炎症及残留毒素活性等问题尚未解决
study_object: 人类/皮肤/特应性皮炎及其他瘙痒性皮肤病/噬菌体衍生内溶素（综述）
disease: 特应性皮炎及其他瘙痒性皮肤病
abstract: Chronic pruritus in atopic dermatitis (AD) is associated with cutaneous dysbiosis, including loss of protective commensals and expansion of Staphylococcus aureus. S. aureus can promote itch through secreted proteases and toxins that activate sensory neurons and amplify type 2 inflammation. Because broad-spectrum antimicrobials may disrupt commensal communities, bacteriophage-derived endolysins have been proposed as a more targeted approach. These enzymes cleave bacterial peptidoglycan and can rapidly lyse susceptible bacteria without requiring active growth, although their antimicrobial spectrum varies by enzyme. Preclinical studies support selective antistaphylococcal activity, but early clinical findings in AD are mixed. Therefore, endolysins should be considered alongside other microbiome-directed approaches, including topical bacteriotherapy with protective commensals. This review evaluates how endolysins work, the available clinical evidence, and the remaining questions about formulation, patient selection, inflammation caused by rapid bacterial breakdown, and toxins that may remain active after the bacteria are killed.

title: Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.
authors: Hu Yongjie; Sun Liuyong; Huang Ye; Jiang Fangfang; Tong Xin et al.
summary_zh: 系统评估优化长读长肠道宏基因组工作流，发现磁板DNA提取结合预处理及长短读长混合组装可提升基因组恢复。
innovation: 系统评估从样本处理到计算组装的长读长宏基因组全流程 | 整合匹配的长读长与短读长数据实现多维度平衡 | 提出长读长优先组装后短读长校正的策略
limitation: 工作流性能仍依赖评价指标 | 未描述
study_object: 人类粪便样本 + 长读长宏基因组测序（CycloneSEQ平台）
abstract: Short-read metagenomic sequencing has been widely applied in microbial research due to its high quality and decreasing cost. However, short reads are inherently fragmented, which limits assembly contiguity and the recovery of complete microbial genomes. In contrast, long-read sequencing, with significantly longer read lengths, helps overcome these limitations. Achieving complete and accurate genome recovery is the core goal of metagenomics. To address this challenge, we systematically evaluated and optimized the long-read metagenomic workflow, from sample processing to computational assembly, using the CycloneSEQ platform.IMPORTANCEOur results suggest that upstream experimental protocols are important contributors to long-read metagenomic performance within the evaluated framework. In particular, magnetic-plate DNA extraction, together with pretreatment, was associated with more favorable input and downstream sequencing-related characteristics for long-read analysis. These changes were also associated with broader microbial recovery in the evaluated data sets. Assembly benchmarking further showed that integrating matched long-read (CycloneSEQ) and short-read (DNBSEQ) data sets provided a favorable balance across multiple evaluation dimensions. In our fecal metagenomic data set, long-read-first assembly followed by short-read polishing showed strong overall performance when recovery, contiguity, and sequence accuracy were considered together, although workflow performance remained metric dependent.

title: Differential metabolite production underlies disruption of the cystic fibrosis airway microbiota by pathogens.
authors: Morabbi Sydney M; Bhowmik Niladri; Sutherland Shaz; Wylie Evelyn A; Decker Reagan S et al.
summary_zh: 重新分析5260份CF气道16S数据并开展共培养实验，发现病原菌通过代谢物抑制其他菌群，破坏微生物组并关联肺功能下降。
innovation: 大规模重新分析5260份16S数据推断微生物互作 | 对96名CF患者分离的1597株菌进行12542次共培养实验验证拮抗作用 | 发现同一供体同一时间点的铜绿假单胞菌分离株代谢组和生物活性存在显著差异并与突变相关
study_object: 囊性纤维化患者/气道/16S rRNA基因测序与共培养实验
sample_size: 5260份16S数据集；96名患者；1597株分离菌；12542次共培养实验
abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) results in accumulation of mucus in the airways that promotes pathogen colonization, leading to respiratory exacerbations, lung failure, and death. The CF airway harbors a complex microbiota, including pathogens and oropharyngeal bacteria. Here, we reanalyzed 5,260 16S rRNA gene microbiota data sets to infer associations between members of the CF microbiota. We determined that pathogens are more likely to proliferate and dominate when present, while oropharyngeal bacteria are generally present at lower abundances. We found that higher diversity and increasing numbers of pairwise associations between bacteria were positively correlated with lung function. In contrast, dominance of the microbiota by pathogens was associated with loss of lung function. We determined that pathogens are largely negatively associated with each other and oropharyngeal bacteria, suggesting they are antagonistic toward other bacteria. As a first test of this hypothesis, we cultured 1,597 isolates from 96 people with CF and performed 12,542 coculture assays against eight representative pathogens and oropharyngeal bacteria, finding 23% of interactions resulted in inhibition. Among our isolates, Pseudomonas were the most inhibitory, but we observed variable activity between different isolates. We further found Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, even those from the same donor and time point, exhibited significant differences in their metabolome and bioactivity profiles that correlated with acquisition of mutations. Together, our results suggest that pathogens may disrupt the CF microbiota and proliferate in part through bioactive metabolite production. Furthermore, these data highlight that characterizing multiple isolates is necessary to capture the full landscape of chemically mediated interactions within microbiomes.IMPORTANCEThe cystic fibrosis (CF) airway harbors a complex microbiota, including oropharyngeal bacteria and opportunistic pathogens that establish chronic infections. We found that microbiota diversity is correlated with health and that a pathogen-dominated microbiota is associated with low lung function. We then inferred potential microbial interactions by determining abundance associations between CF genera, which suggested that pathogens antagonize other bacteria. To test this prediction, we cultured bacteria from people with CF and performed thousands of coculture assays, finding that approximately one-quarter of interactions resulted in growth inhibition. Pseudomonas broadly inhibited other members of the CF airway microbiota. However, we observed marked variability in bioactivity and metabolite profiles of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates, even from the same donor at the same time. Our results suggest that pathogens disrupt the CF microbiota, possibly through bioactive metabolite production, and that characterizing multiple isolates is necessary to capture the complete picture of interactions in these communities.

title: Metabolic reprogramming of myeloid‑derived suppressor cells in colorectal cancer: Mechanistic insights and immunometabolic targeted rehabilitation (Review).
authors: Zhu Liang-Xiao; Jiang Guang-Jie; Gao Feng-Hou; Du Yi-Qiao
summary_zh: 综述探讨结直肠癌中髓源性抑制细胞代谢重编程机制，提出靶向代谢脆弱性的免疫代谢康复框架以转化其表型。
innovation: 提出“突变-代谢-抑制”自强化轴 | 强调空间代谢拮抗及肠道/瘤内菌群代谢物远程调控MDSC | 提出免疫代谢康复框架整合空间组学、AI药物设计与菌群调控
study_object: 结直肠癌患者/肿瘤微环境+髓源性抑制细胞+综述
abstract: Metabolic reprogramming of myeloid‑derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) plays a role in immunotherapy resistance in colorectal cancer (CRC). This metabolic reprogramming appears to be coordinated by oncogenic mutations (such as adenomatous polyposis coli, KRAS and TP53) through a proposed self‑reinforcing 'mutation‑metabolism‑suppression' axis. In the present review, four core metabolic pillars sustaining MDSC pathogenicity and the epimetabolic regulation that durably locks them into a suppressive state were examined. Furthermore, two emerging dimensions were highlighted: The spatial metabolic antagonism through which MDSCs may construct a metabolically hostile zone to limit the functional activity of tertiary lymphoid structures, and the remote manipulation of MDSC function by gut and intratumoral microbiota‑derived metabolites. To transcend the limitations of non‑specific myeloid depletion, immunometabolic rehabilitation is proposed as a potentially transformative framework targeting intrinsic metabolic vulnerabilities to functionally reprogram MDSCs from an immunosuppressive to a homeostatic or immunostimulatory phenotype. By integrating emerging spatial omics for precise target validation, artificial intelligence‑guided rational drug design and microbiome modulation, this paradigm provides a strategic roadmap for next‑generation precision immunotherapy, aiming to achieve durable responses across both microsatellite stable and microsatellite instability‑high CRC.

title: Advances in HIV-associated pulmonary diseases: an official American Thoracic Society workshop report.
journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
authors: North Crystal M; Konstantinidis Ioannis; Attia Engi F; Auld Sara C; Cho Josalyn L et al.
summary_zh: 该 workshop 报告总结 HIV 感染者肺部疾病研究进展，指出免疫失调、氧化应激、衰老和微生物组改变等机制，呼吁全球协作和精准防治。
innovation: 强调微生物组改变是 HIV 相关肺病的复杂机制之一 | 提出整合多组学和纵向表型分析以推动精准防治 | 采用改良德尔菲法组织跨转化研究专家共识
limitation: HIV 特异性临床试验有限 | 肺病研究中 HIV 感染者代表性不足，且撒哈拉以南非洲及儿童青少年数据差异大
study_object: HIV感染者/肺部疾病/多组学与纵向表型分析
abstract: People with HIV (PWH) are at increased risk of a broad range of infectious and non-infectious pulmonary diseases. Since the last ATS Workshop on HIV-associated pulmonary disease, large national and international cohorts have demonstrated ongoing gaps in our understanding of lung disease in this vulnerable population that range from underappreciation of disease incidence and prevalence to lack of targeted treatments. Translational work on the underlying mechanisms of disease has demonstrated novel, HIV-specific mechanisms that may lend themselves to tailored therapies. Twenty-four experts in HIV-associated lung disease from across the translational spectrum were invited to participate in this ATS-sponsored Workshop utilizing a modified Delphi method that included a series of pre- and post-workshop electronic surveys and a two-day virtual workshop. Lung disease among PWH is driven by complex and interrelated mechanisms including persistent immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, accelerated aging, and microbiome alterations. Despite these advances in our understanding, important gaps persist between mechanistic insights and clinical care that include limited HIV-specific trials, underrepresentation of PWH in studies of lung disease, and the absence of tailored care strategies. These gaps are further accentuated by substantial variation in the availability of data from the most affected populations, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and among children and adolescents. Overcoming these challenges will require coordinated, globally representative research efforts that leverage large cohorts, integrate multi-omics and longitudinal phenotyping, use mechanistic insights to inform clinical trials, and consider implementation science approaches with the ultimate goal of developing tailored prevention and treatment strategies for HIV-associated pulmonary diseases.

title: Enriched microplastic-associated biofilms exacerbate gut microbial dysbiosis and metabolic disruption in mice.
authors: Li Shan; Chen Tingqin; Liu Jiajia; Lu Kunman; Chen Xuemei et al.
summary_zh: 研究评估微塑料表面富集生物膜对小鼠肠道菌群和代谢的影响，发现其导致菌群失调和代谢紊乱。
innovation: 评估微塑料表面富集生物膜对哺乳动物的健康风险 | 结合宏基因组和代谢组分析宿主响应
study_object: 小鼠/肠道/宏基因组与代谢组
disease: 肠道菌群失调和代谢紊乱
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and opportunistic pathogens are recognized as emerging environmental hazards, yet the health risks associated with mammalian exposure to biofilms enriched on MP surfaces remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the characteristics of microbial biofilms enriched on MPs from aquatic and sediment matrices over 12 weeks and assessed their potential health impacts using a murine mammalian model. Metagenomic profiling showed that the enriched biofilms exhibited alterations in community composition, accompanied by an overrepresentation of genes associated with antibiotic resistance, iron acquisition, and virulence traits. In the murine model, dietary exposure to the MP-associated biofilms coincided with changes in host intestinal inflammatory markers and a distinct shift in the gut microbiota profile. Metabolomic analysis further revealed synchronous alterations in extracellular and fecal metabolite profiles, including profiles linked to secondary bile acid pathways, alongside a downregulation of intestinal barrier tight junction markers. These parallel taxonomic and metabolic shifts indicate that environmental biofilms enriched on microplastics can provoke complex physiological responses in a mammalian host. This study provides a valuable framework for assessing the potential mammalian health risks posed by plastisphere-associated microbial complexes.

title: Phocaeicola vulgatus alleviates obesity through cross-species arginine production and hepatic retinoic acid signaling.
authors: Li Yushi; Li Jinmei; Deng Jiteng; Xia Pei; Zhou Guicheng et al.
summary_zh: 通过临床队列和菌群移植大鼠模型，发现P. vulgatus通过促进精氨酸合成和肝脏视黄酸信号缓解肥胖。
innovation: 揭示P. vulgatus与P. faecium协同增强肠道精氨酸生物合成 | 首次将P. vulgatus、循环精氨酸与肝脏视黄酸信号联系起来阐明抗肥胖机制
study_object: 人类（肥胖与瘦个体）粪便样本及人源化大鼠模型；宏基因组、代谢组和转录组技术
abstract: Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) shows inconsistent clinical efficacy in treating obesity, and the specific microbial determinants dictating its success remain poorly characterized. Our previous clinical FMT trial identified Phocaeicola vulgatus as a key microbe contributing to the therapeutic efficacy of obesity treatment. Here, to investigate its role in obesity, we established an independent clinical cohort comprising obese and lean individuals, revealing that the P. vulgatus-centered network and ornithine synthesis are impaired in the obese group. We then confirmed causality by utilizing a humanized rat model carrying microbiota from a P. vulgatus-deficient obese patient, demonstrating that P. vulgatus supplementation significantly mitigates HFD-induced obesity, including reductions in body weight and serum total cholesterol levels, as well as the alleviation of hepatic steatosis. To further explore the functional mechanisms of P. vulgatus, integrated metagenomic and metabolomic analyses revealed a potential functional association between P. vulgatus and Phascolarctobacterium faecium that is associated with enhanced intestinal arginine biosynthesis and systemic availability. Furthermore, hepatic transcriptomics linked these elevated circulating arginine levels to the upregulation of retinoic acid (RA) signaling. Taken together, our findings outline a potential microbial-host network wherein P. vulgatus mitigates obesity via the arginine-RA axis, providing a valuable scientific basis for exploring this strain as a probiotic candidate for metabolic health.

title: Agaricus bisporus polysaccharides alleviate high-fat diet-induced cognitive impairment via microbiota-gut-brain axis modulation.
authors: Fu Chujing; Ye Kai; Qiu Zhichang; Hu Xinyu; Wang Xiaoxuan et al.
summary_zh: 本研究探讨双孢蘑菇多糖对高脂饮食诱导认知障碍的保护作用，发现其改善小鼠认知、神经炎症和菌群-肠-脑轴。
innovation: 揭示双孢蘑菇多糖通过菌群-肠-脑轴缓解高脂饮食认知障碍 | 发现ABP富集Akkermansia和Bacteroides并增加短链脂肪酸产生
study_object: 小鼠 + 高脂饮食模型 + 肠道菌群和短链脂肪酸分析
disease: 高脂饮食诱导的认知障碍
abstract: This study aimed to explore the protective effect of Agaricus bisporus polysaccharide (ABP) against high-fat diet (HFD) induced cognitive impairment (CI), with a particular focus on gut-brain communication. ABP supplementation alleviated anxiety-like behavior and cognitive deficits in HFD-fed mice. These effects were associated with enhanced hippocampal synaptic plasticity and attenuated inflammatory responses, which were accompanied by the elevation of Bdnf levels and the upregulated expression of plasticity-related genes (e.g., Gria2, Grin2b, Tdp2, and Fxr1). Crucially, ABP supplementation was associated with alleviated HFD-induced morphological changes in microglia and reduced inflammatory factor mRNA levels (Tnf, Il1b). Meanwhile, ABP remodeled the gut microbiome, significantly enriching beneficial taxa including Akkermansia and Bacteroides and enhancing the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), mainly acetate and propionate. These findings suggest that ABP may serve as a promising nutritional component for alleviating diet-related CI with effect associated with modulation of the microbiota-gut-brain axis.

title: Machine learning prediction of human antibiotic resistance risk using 16S rRNA profiles.
authors: Zhang Qi; Wang Zeling; Lei Chaotang; Xu Nuohan; Zhang Zhenyan et al.
summary_zh: 研究通过整合宏基因组与16S数据构建ARG宿主目录，用机器学习从微生物组成预测抗生素耐药风险，模型精度高且跨平台可迁移。
innovation: 整合大规模宏基因组和16S数据定义ARG宿主目录与核心分类群 | 建立从16S分类组成定量推断抗生素耐药风险的机器学习框架 | 证明宿主相关生态因素比社会经济条件解释更多耐药风险变异
study_object: 人类 + 宏基因组和16S rRNA样本 + 机器学习
sample_size: 177,134个宏基因组组装基因组、3058个宏基因组、31,216个16S rRNA谱
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a growing global health threat, yet large-scale surveillance and risk evaluation remain constrained by the cost and accessibility of metagenomic sequencing. Here, we demonstrate that antibiotic resistance risk, integrating gene mobility, human accessibility, clinical relevance, and host pathogenicity, can be quantitatively inferred from microbial taxonomic composition through its ecological coupling with microbial hosts. By integrating 177,134 metagenome-assembled genomes, 3058 metagenomes, and 31,216 16S rRNA profiles, we defined a comprehensive ARG host catalogue and conserved core taxa across sequencing platforms. A machine learning model built on this framework achieved high predictive accuracy in held-out test data (R2 > 0.96) and retained strong performance in an independent dataset with paired 16S rRNA and metagenomic profiles (Pearson r = 0.74; Lin's CCC = 0.73), supporting its robustness and cross-platform transferability. Applying this tool on a global scale, we demonstrate that resistance risk exhibits consistent structure across populations, with host-associated ecological factors explaining more variation than socioeconomic conditions, supporting the feasibility of translating taxonomic profiles into quantitative estimates of functional risk. This work establishes a scalable framework for inferring antibiotic resistance risk from 16S data, enabling equitable, large-scale surveillance of antimicrobial resistance while positioning microbiome composition as a predictive basis for functional risk and advancing a general paradigm for inferring microbial traits from community structure.

title: Maternal co-exposure to polystyrene microplastics and DEHP impairs thyroid function in adult rat offspring.
authors: Zhang Xin; Li Jiangli; Yang Zelong; Zheng Sida; Huang Qianhui et al.
summary_zh: 孕期大鼠共暴露PS-MPs和DEHP致子代甲状腺功能紊乱，伴肠道菌群改变，存在性别差异。
innovation: 揭示两种污染物共暴露对子代甲状腺的加和与协同毒性 | 提出肠-脑-甲状腺轴扰动模型 | 强调性别特异性易感性及混合物风险评估必要性
study_object: 大鼠/孕期及哺乳期母体暴露/子代甲状腺与肠道菌群/16S rRNA基因测序（微生物组 profiling）
disease: 甲状腺内分泌干扰（甲状腺功能紊乱）
abstract: Maternal combined exposure to polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) and di-(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) poses potential risks to offspring endocrine development; however, the combined effects of these two contaminants remain poorly characterized. Pregnant rats were exposed to PS-MPs, DEHP, or a combination of both throughout pregnancy and lactation. The hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis function and gut microbiota composition were then assessed in adult offspring. Single-contaminant exposure altered thyroid hormone levels and HPT axis gene expression. Co-exposure exacerbated these disruptions, producing greater TSH suppression, elevated thyroid hormone levels, and uniform downregulation of Nis expression in offspring of both sexes. Sex-specific differences in hypothalamic and pituitary gene expression were observed, suggesting that upstream HPT axis regulation was disrupted via sex-divergent mechanisms. The combined exposure also induced morphological disruption of thyroid follicular epithelial cells and elevated oxidative stress markers. In co-exposed offspring, gut microbiome profiling revealed Bacteroides depletion and Enterococcus enrichment as the most prominent taxa-level shifts. The parallel perturbations in gut microbiome composition and HPT axis function across treatment groups support a proposed disruption model of the gut-brain-thyroid axis. Our findings demonstrate that maternal co-exposure to PS-MPs and DEHP induces sex-divergent thyroid endocrine disruption in offspring, driven by a complex integration of additive and synergistic toxicities.
